steps.intent: The United States’ objective is to renew the MSS authorization while anchoring it in Haitian ownership, electoral preparation by February 2026, and stronger sanctions implementation; the draft avoids immediate creation of a new UN peacekeeping operation and emphasizes voluntary, burden-shared support. The main difficulties will be Russian and Chinese concerns about broad Chapter VII enforcement language, cost and UN assumptions, and human rights accountability following recent allegations against Haitian police and the drone strike. To secure passage, the text is time-limited, reporting-heavy, and conditions any transition on consultation and future Council review.

Add new operative paragraph: 'Underlines that the security situation in Haiti requires a comprehensive approach addressing its root causes, and calls upon Member States and international partners to scale up humanitarian assistance and support for reconstruction, food security and socioeconomic development in Haiti;'

China.change: Replace 'options for a possible transition from the MSS to a United Nations peacekeeping operation' with 'options for the possible future role of the United Nations in sustaining security and stability in Haiti, including a peacekeeping operation only if conditions on the ground permit, with the consent of the Government of Haiti and pursuant to a decision of the Security Council'; add that any transition must be conditions-based, gradual and not automatic.

Add after 'information-sharing': 'and further requests the Sanctions Committee to strengthen monitoring and reporting on the arms embargo, including illicit trafficking and diversion networks, and calls on all Member States, especially neighboring States, to enhance border controls and prevent arms and ammunition from reaching armed gangs.'

Denmark.change: Strengthen the accountability and civilian-harm provisions: request the MSS, in consultation with BINUH, OHCHR and Haitian civil society, to establish robust civilian-harm mitigation, misconduct investigation and accountability mechanisms, and to report to the Council through the Secretary-General on their operation and outcomes, while ensuring full compliance with the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy.

Add a humanitarian carve-out and stronger arms-embargo implementation language: 'Reaffirms that the measures imposed by resolutions 2699 (2023), 2700 (2023) and 2752 (2024) do not apply to the provision of humanitarian assistance and other activities consistent with resolution 2664 (2022), and calls for strengthened border and cargo inspection cooperation to prevent arms trafficking.'

Expand the reporting requirements to include civilian harm, violations of international humanitarian law, implementation of the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, humanitarian access, and arms-embargo violations, and to reflect BINUH and Haitian civil-society input.

Add an early review trigger: express the Council's intention to review the MSS authorization upon the Secretary-General's report due by 15 January 2026, and to consider adjustments to the mandate, size, composition or transition timeline in light of conditions on the ground.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of the MSS and the Council's unified response to the crisis in Haiti. However, the text must explicitly anchor the Mission in the consent of the Government of Haiti and Haiti's sovereignty; it should also address predictable financing and a clear exit strategy. Algeria further calls for stronger emphasis on humanitarian assistance and root causes. We can support the draft with these changes.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the MSS and remains committed to Haiti’s sovereignty and a Haitian-led solution. We can join consensus if OP7 makes clear that any transition to a UN peacekeeping operation is conditions-based, consensual and not automatic, and if the text strengthens implementation of the arms embargo. We also ask for explicit consent language in OP2 and for reporting to be based on verified information and consultation with the Haitian Government.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports extending the MSS authorization, given the dire security and humanitarian situation, and welcomes the strong human-rights and civilian-protection language already in the draft. We would like the accountability and civilian-harm provisions in OP3 strengthened, and we ask the penholders to add a humanitarian carve-out to the sanctions, expand reporting on civilian harm and arms-embargo implementation, and provide for an early review after the January 2026 report. These changes are important for Denmark's support because they align the mandate with international law, humanitarian access and effective Council oversight.
messages.France: France supports the extension of the MSS and commends the penholders for their work. We ask for targeted additions on BINUH’s role in strengthening judicial and penal systems, the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth in the political transition, and options for predictable and sustainable financing for the MSS and the Haitian National Police. We also want OP7 to cover the full range of UN support options, not only a peacekeeping transition, so the Council can decide in January on the basis of the Secretary-General’s recommendations.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the extension of the MSS and the Council’s strong reaffirmation of Haitian sovereignty and the Haitian-led political transition. We would ask for targeted strengthening of human rights accountability and child protection/WPS provisions in the mandate and reporting, as well as clearer reporting on humanitarian access and displacement. These changes would make the text more operationally credible and consistent with Greece’s priorities on international law and protection of civilians.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft as a basis for renewing the MSS and welcomes its focus on Haitian leadership, civilian protection and sanctions implementation. We ask the penholders to strengthen language on predictable and sustainable financing, root causes, and a conditions-based transition with CARICOM consultation. We also seek child-protection and reintegration safeguards in the DDR provisions. Guyana can support the text with these improvements.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the renewal of the MSS and the draft’s Haitian-led orientation. We ask the penholder to make explicit that the extension and operations are at the request and with the consent of the Government of Haiti, and to include language on predictable and sustainable financing. We also seek TCC consultations and clear benchmarks and timelines for any transition to a UN peacekeeping operation, consistent with conditions on the ground, while ensuring sanctions do not impede humanitarian assistance.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the United States for its work as co-penholder and supports extending the MSS authorization. We ask that the February 2026 electoral goal be tied to conditions on the ground, and that BINUH be explicitly associated with electoral coordination. We also seek safeguards in OP6 so that support to the MSS does not come at the expense of BINUH’s mandate and resources.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the draft and commends the penholder for advancing the MSS mandate and transition planning. We would like the text to explicitly strengthen HNP capacity and professionalization, and to call for predictable, sustained and adequate funding for the MSS. We also ask that OP7 make clear that any transition to a UN peacekeeping operation is conditions-based and subject to the consent of the Government of Haiti.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation can support the extension of the MSS, as we did in 2024, provided the text clearly reaffirms that the Mission operates at the request and with the ongoing consent of the Haitian Government and does not create any automatic pathway to a United Nations peacekeeping operation. We ask the penholders to add clear benchmarks and an exit strategy for the MSS and to strengthen language on tackling the external sources and transfer routes of illicit arms into Haiti. Any future transition must be subject to a further decision of the Security Council and conditions on the ground.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the draft as a basis and welcomes the extension of the MSS authorization. We ask the penholders to strengthen predictable financing for the MSS, include concrete proposals for enhancing BINUH’s role in the political transition and enforcement action, and reinforce WPS participation and arms-embargo enforcement. These changes would align the text with the A3+ concerns and the Secretary-General’s recommendations.
messages.Slovenia: We welcome the draft and can support its direction. We would ask for focused improvements on child protection in disarmament and reintegration, reporting on arms-embargo implementation, and a January review aligned with the Secretary-General's report and the BINUH mandate. These changes would strengthen implementation and accountability without altering the core mandate.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the extension of the MSS and the draft’s emphasis on Haitian ownership and protection of civilians. Given our own experience with underfunded security missions, we ask the penholders to strengthen language on predictable and sustainable financing, including assessed contributions, and to ensure transition planning is done in close consultation with Haiti and troop- and police-contributing countries. We can support the text with those adjustments.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks the United States and Panama for the draft and supports renewal of the MSS. We would like to see the text strengthen women's and civil society participation in elections, independent and transparent accountability, and safe, rapid and sustained humanitarian access. We also ask for clearer reporting on sexual and gender-based violence, child recruitment, human rights due diligence and civilian harm, plus minor language on maritime arms trafficking.

replies.Algeria: partially accepted: consent, exit strategy and root causes included; financing options retained without explicit assessed contributions
replies.Guyana: partially accepted: assessed contributions not endorsed; financing exploration and child safeguards included
replies.Pakistan: partially accepted: financing exploration included; assessed contributions not endorsed
replies.Sierra Leone: partially accepted: BINUH proposals and arms/WPS language included; assessed contributions not endorsed
replies.Somalia: partially accepted: TCC consultation included; assessed contributions not endorsed

steps.summary: The United States has revised the text to retain the MSS authorization while adding consent, conditions-based transition, stronger sanctions implementation, human-rights accountability, WPS and child-protection safeguards, and reporting. Explicit assessed contributions were not endorsed, but financing options and reporting were included to preserve consensus. The revised draft is expected to command unanimous support.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the penholder for incorporating consent, exit strategy and root causes in the text. We still believe the financing language should be more predictable and should explicitly allow consideration of assessed contributions, given the Mission's chronic shortfalls. We also request a dedicated operative paragraph operationalizing root-cause support through humanitarian, food security and socioeconomic assistance. Algeria is ready to work constructively on compromise language and can support the text with these improvements.
messages.China: China supports the current draft and thanks the penholder for accepting our previous requests, which have strengthened respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, consent and the arms embargo. The text maintains a conditions-based approach to any future UN role and preserves BINUH’s political mandate. China is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the penholder for incorporating our key proposals on civilian-harm mitigation, HRDDP, the humanitarian carve-out, arms-embargo implementation, and enhanced reporting and review. The current text reflects a balanced, conditions-based and rights-sensitive approach that Denmark can support. We encourage the Council to speak with one voice and remain ready to support the draft as it stands.
messages.France: France supports the current text and thanks the penholders for incorporating our earlier concerns on BINUH’s role, participation, financing options and the range of possible UN support arrangements. The draft provides a robust, conditions-based mandate for the MSS while strengthening human rights, child protection and accountability. France can support adoption as drafted and encourages the Council to remain actively seized of implementation and sustainable financing.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the current draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier proposals on human rights training, civilian oversight, child protection, WPS expertise and sex- and age-disaggregated reporting. The text strikes a balanced approach by reinforcing Haitian ownership and consent while strengthening accountability, humanitarian access and the sanctions regime. We encourage the Council to maintain this unified position and to remain seized of implementation and transition planning.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the revised draft and appreciates the incorporation of root causes, child protection safeguards, and a conditions-based, phased transition in close consultation with CARICOM. We still seek one change in OP5: make explicit that the financing options to be explored include assessed contributions, as the A3+ has consistently called for. We do not treat this as a red line, but it remains important for predictable and sustainable financing of the MSS.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft and appreciates the inclusion of Haitian consent, humanitarian carve-outs, and consultation with troop- and police-contributing countries. To address the MSS's chronic funding shortfalls, we request that OP5 explicitly include assessed contributions among the financing options to be explored and reported on by the Secretary-General. With that reflected, Pakistan can support the text.
messages.Panama: Panama welcomes the incorporation of our amendments on the conditions-based political timeline, BINUH coordination in electoral support, and safeguarding BINUH’s mandate and resources. We support the text as it stands and call for its adoption.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks the penholder and co-sponsors for the revised text and welcomes the incorporation of its proposals on Haitian National Police professionalization, predictable and sustainable financing, and a conditions-based transition. We support the current draft and encourage the Council to remain united in supporting a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned response, with continued attention to human rights due diligence and sustainable international support.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the revised draft. Our key concerns have been reflected: the mandate is at the request and with the ongoing consent of the Government of Haiti, any future transition is conditions-based and subject to a further Council decision, and the text addresses external arms flows and benchmarks. We will vote in favour.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised draft and welcomes the incorporation of the BINUH proposals and stronger arms-embargo and WPS language. We remain concerned that voluntary financing has not matched the MSS's mandated tasks, so OP5 should explicitly include assessed contributions among the financing options to be explored. With that amendment, we are ready to support the text.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes revision 1 and the incorporation of our earlier proposals on child protection, arms-embargo reporting, WPS and child protection reporting, and the review clause. We consider the text balanced and firmly grounded in Haitian ownership, human rights due diligence, and accountability. Slovenia therefore supports the draft as it stands and calls for its adoption.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft and welcomes the inclusion of troop- and police-contributing countries in the financing and transition consultations. However, the text still does not explicitly capture assessed contributions as a financing option, which Somalia considers important for predictable and sustainable support to the MSS and the Haitian National Police. We ask the penholder to add this reference in OP5 and can support the text with that addition.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the revised draft and has no further changes to request. We welcome the incorporation of our priorities on humanitarian access, women’s participation, civilian harm mitigation and reporting, and we encourage all Council members to join consensus. A unified Council message is essential for supporting Haiti’s security, political transition and accountability efforts.

replies.Algeria: partially accepted: added new root-cause/humanitarian paragraph; OP5 now includes assessed contributions with an 'as appropriate' qualifier.
replies.Guyana: partially accepted: OP5 now includes assessed contributions with an 'as appropriate' qualifier.
replies.Pakistan: accepted: OP5 includes 'assessed contributions, as appropriate' among financing options to explore.
replies.Sierra Leone: partially accepted: OP5 now references funding, equipment and logistical shortfalls and includes assessed contributions with a qualifier.
replies.Somalia: partially accepted: OP5 now includes assessed contributions with an 'as appropriate' qualifier.

steps.summary: The revision accepts Algeria's root-cause/humanitarian paragraph and reflects A3+ calls on assessed contributions through qualified language in OP5, while preserving voluntary contributions and the conditions-based approach. This keeps the broad coalition supportive, including all permanent members, and is expected to be adopted unanimously.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria had requested changes that were partially accepted, and its consistent record is to support Haiti resolutions. It would vote in favour while explaining sovereignty, financing, and root-cause concerns.
reasons.China: China’s position in the final negotiation round was support, and the revised text accommodates its emphasis on sovereignty, Haitian ownership, a conditions-based transition and implementation of the arms embargo. Consistent with its prior votes on extending the MSS, China will vote in favour.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supported the draft in negotiations and its priorities on human rights safeguards, humanitarian access, and a conditions-based transition are reflected. Voting yes is consistent with Denmark's strong support for multilateral crisis response and the Haitian-led political process.
reasons.France: France has consistently supported the MSS and BINUH, has contributed financially and politically, and the draft reflects its priorities on sustainable financing, sanctions, human rights due diligence and Haitian sovereignty. No elements require abstention or veto.
reasons.Greece: Greece has consistently supported Haiti resolutions and indicated support for this draft, with no outstanding requests. As an elected member, it would back a text that reinforces humanitarian access, sanctions implementation and human rights safeguards while preserving Haitian ownership.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported Security Council mandates on Haiti and the MSS, and its key financing request was partially reflected in OP5, so voting in favour is consistent with its position. A brief explanation before the vote allows Guyana to record its support while noting the remaining financing caveat.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan supported the draft because its key request on assessed contributions was accommodated, and the text affirms Haitian sovereignty, consent, civilian protection and a conditions-based transition consistent with Pakistan’s established position on Haiti and UN peace and security operations.
reasons.Panama: Panama co-sponsored the draft and has consistently supported BINUH, the MSS, sanctions and a Haitian-led transition. Voting in favour with a rights- and sovereignty-focused explanation is consistent with its recent record.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported Security Council action on Haiti, including the MSS and BINUH, and the draft aligns with its emphasis on Haitian-led solutions, civilian protection, human rights compliance, and sustainable financing. It therefore votes in favour and explains its support before the vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia has supported recent Haiti resolutions and entered the final round supporting this draft; its concerns about future peacekeeping and financing are addressed through further Council decisions rather than automatic commitments. Moscow can therefore vote yes while publicly emphasizing arms trafficking and Haitian-led political transition.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone’s priority request on OP5 was partially accepted, and the draft is consistent with its record of supporting BINUH and the MSS while advancing A3+ concerns on financing, sanctions, and Haitian ownership; it would therefore vote in favour while flagging remaining concerns.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia has consistently supported Security Council resolutions on Haiti and the draft reflects its priorities on civilian protection, human rights due diligence, child protection, WPS, accountability, and sustainable financing. There is no reason to abstain or oppose.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia supported previous Haiti resolutions and its key financing request was partially accommodated; voting in favour is consistent with its support for UN-backed security and predictable mission financing. The statement underscores sovereignty, humanitarian access, sanctions and conditions-based review.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom has consistently supported previous MSS mandates and the draft reflects its priorities on human rights compliance, sanctions enforcement, and conditions-based planning for any future UN role. Voting in favour reinforces Council unity and the call for full implementation.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is the penholder and co-sponsor with Panama, so it strongly supports the draft and seeks its adoption. The text advances core U.S. priorities on Haiti: MSS authorization, sanctions enforcement, humanitarian access, and a conditions-based path toward future UN options.

before.Algeria: Algeria votes in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the incorporation of language on the root causes of the crisis, humanitarian assistance and socio-economic development, as well as the reference to assessed contributions as appropriate, which we had sought in the negotiations. At the same time, we stress that the Multinational Security Support Mission must act with full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, consent and territorial integrity, in strict compliance with international law and the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. We also emphasise the need for predictable and sustainable financing, full implementation of the arms embargo, and a credible, inclusive and Haitian-led political transition leading to elections. Algeria remains committed to supporting the people and Government of Haiti in restoring security, stability and development.
before.China: China supports the draft resolution and will vote in favour. We welcome the text’s reaffirmation of Haiti’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, as well as its emphasis on a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned process. We also note the provisions on the Multinational Security Support Mission’s authorization being conditions-based, gradual and subject to further Council review, and we stress that the Mission must fully respect Haitian sovereignty, international law and the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. China calls for full implementation of the arms embargo and for concrete action against the illicit trafficking of weapons into Haiti. The international community should provide predictable and sustainable support to Haiti while respecting the country’s ownership, and the Security Council should continue to review the situation on the basis of conditions on the ground.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this resolution. We thank the United States and Panama for their work. The people of Haiti face an urgent security and humanitarian crisis, and this Council must support a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned response. Denmark supports the extension of the Multinational Security Support Mission with clear safeguards on human rights, child protection, civilian harm mitigation and accountability. We stress the need for predictable financing, full implementation of the arms embargo, unhindered humanitarian access, and the safe, full and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society in the political transition. Denmark also underlines that any future transition to a United Nations peacekeeping operation or other arrangement must be conditions-based, gradual, with the consent of the Government of Haiti, and subject to a further decision of this Council.
before.France: France votes in favour of this draft resolution. The Multinational Security Support Mission is essential to protecting civilians, supporting the Haitian National Police and creating conditions for a credible political transition. We welcome the provisions on predictable financing, full implementation of the sanctions regime, Haitian ownership and respect for human rights, including robust civilian harm mitigation and accountability. France will continue to support BINUH, the Haitian authorities and the holding of inclusive and credible elections.
before.Greece: Thank you, Mr. President. Greece will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the continuation of the Multinational Security Support Mission within a clear framework that upholds Haiti’s sovereignty and leadership and places the protection of civilians, human rights compliance and accountability at the centre of its work. We particularly welcome the emphasis on the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, child protection, the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, and the need for predictable financing. We also stress that any future transition to a United Nations peacekeeping operation must be conditions-based, gradual and subject to a further decision of this Council. Greece remains committed to a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process that addresses the root causes of the crisis and creates the conditions for credible elections and lasting stability.
before.Guyana: Guyana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the extension of the Multinational Security Support Mission and its close coordination with the Haitian National Police and BINUH, in full respect of Haiti’s sovereignty and in support of a Haitian-led political transition. We welcome the inclusion in paragraph 5 of assessed contributions, as appropriate, although we would have preferred a more robust formulation. Predictable and sustainable financing remains essential for the Mission’s effectiveness. We also stress the importance of full implementation of the sanctions regime and of intensified efforts against illicit arms trafficking. Guyana will continue to stand with the people and Government of Haiti and with regional partners, including CARICOM, in addressing this multidimensional crisis.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the penholders for engaging with our proposal on predictable and sustainable financing, reflected in paragraph 5 through the reference to assessed contributions, as appropriate. Pakistan reiterates that the crisis in Haiti requires a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned response, with full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and consent. We support the extension of the MSS to help protect civilians, restore public order and support the Haitian National Police, while stressing the need for robust implementation of the arms embargo, protection of children and vulnerable persons, accountability and civilian harm mitigation, and a conditions-based approach to any future transition. We also emphasize that sustainable financing, including assessed contributions as appropriate, should be seriously explored so that the mission is not left dependent on uncertain voluntary contributions.
before.Panama: Panamá se pronuncia a favor de este proyecto de resolución, que copatrocinamos. La grave situación de seguridad y humanitaria en Haití exige una respuesta internacional sostenida, coordinada y plenamente respetuosa de la soberanía haitiana y del liderazgo del Gobierno y del pueblo de Haití. Acompañamos la prórroga de la Misión Multinacional de Apoyo a la Seguridad porque puede contribuir a proteger a la población civil, apoyar a la Policía Nacional de Haití, facilitar la asistencia humanitaria y sentar condiciones para una transición política creíble hacia elecciones. Al mismo tiempo, subrayamos la importancia de la coordinación con la BINUH, el pleno cumplimiento del derecho internacional y de la debida diligencia en materia de derechos humanos, la protección de la niñez, la prevención de la explotación y abusos sexuales, la rendición de cuentas y la participación plena, igualitaria y significativa de las mujeres, los jóvenes y la sociedad civil. Asimismo, reiteramos la necesidad de aplicar efectivamente el régimen de sanciones y de combatir el tráfico ilícito de armas, así como de dotar a la Misión de financiamiento previsible y sostenible. La transición a cualquier arreglo futuro deberá ser gradual, basada en condiciones, sujeta al consentimiento de Haití y a una nueva decisión del Consejo. Panamá votará a favor.
before.Republic of Korea:
The Republic of Korea votes in favour of this resolution. We remain deeply concerned by the continued deterioration of the security and humanitarian situation in Haiti, including the expansion of gang control, widespread displacement, hunger, and grave violations against civilians, especially children and women. We support the extension of the Multinational Security Support Mission so that it can continue to assist the Haitian National Police in protecting civilians, restoring public order, securing humanitarian access, and preparing the conditions for an inclusive, Haitian-led political transition leading to elections.

At the same time, international security support cannot be a substitute for a durable Haitian-owned political solution. We underscore the importance of full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, strict compliance with international human rights and humanitarian law, robust civilian harm mitigation and accountability mechanisms, and the protection of children formerly associated with armed gangs as victims. We also stress the need for predictable and sustainable financing, equipment and logistical support for the Mission and the Haitian National Police, and for enhanced implementation of the arms embargo and sanctions regime to cut off the illicit flows that fuel gang violence. The Republic of Korea will continue to support Haiti and to work with Council members and regional partners, including CARICOM, in pursuit of stability and a credible political transition.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support continuing international assistance to Haiti in stabilizing the security situation on the basis of Haiti’s sovereignty, consent and ownership. At the same time, we stress that force alone cannot resolve the crisis. The Council must give priority to cutting off illicit arms trafficking, including external arms flows that continue to fuel gang violence, and to advancing an inclusive, Haitian-led political process leading to elections. We also proceed from the understanding that any possible future transition to a United Nations peacekeeping operation must be strictly conditions-based and subject to a further decision of the Security Council, without automaticity. We will continue to monitor the implementation of the mandate closely.
before.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone votes in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the penholders for their efforts and welcome the partial incorporation of our proposal in operative paragraph 5 on more predictable and sustainable financing for the Multinational Security Support Mission, including reference to assessed contributions. We would have preferred stronger language on this point, but we support the extension of the MSS mandate, stress the need for full implementation of the sanctions and arms embargo, and call for continued protection of civilians, accountability, and a Haitian-led political transition.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the penholders for their efforts and the constructive engagement on this text. We vote in favour of the resolution. The situation in Haiti remains deeply alarming, and the Council must act with a clear purpose: to protect civilians, uphold human rights, support the safe delivery of humanitarian assistance, and advance a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political transition. We welcome the strengthened provisions on civilian harm mitigation, accountability, the protection of children, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society. We stress that the mandate must be implemented in full respect for international law, including human rights law and international humanitarian law, and with full application of the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. Sustainable and predictable financing for the Multinational Security Support Mission and the Haitian National Police is essential; voluntary contributions alone remain insufficient. We also underline the need for robust implementation of the arms embargo and enhanced regional cooperation to stop illicit arms flows. Any future transition to a United Nations peacekeeping operation must be conditions-based, gradual, with clear benchmarks and the consent of the Government of Haiti. Slovenia remains committed to supporting the people of Haiti and a comprehensive, rights-based response to this crisis.
before.Somalia: Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the extension of the Multinational Security Support Mission and the inclusion of assessed contributions, as appropriate, among the options for more predictable and sustainable financing. We stress that international action must remain Haitian-led and Haitian-owned, with full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, and must prioritize protection of civilians, unimpeded humanitarian access, robust implementation of the arms embargo, accountability and a conditions-based transition with clear benchmarks and regular review. We also call for close coordination with CARICOM and regional partners, and for the Secretary-General’s reporting to remain transparent and grounded in verified information.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. We thank the United States and Panama for their leadership. The United Kingdom remains deeply concerned by the worsening security and humanitarian situation in Haiti, the expansion of gang control, and the illicit trafficking of arms and ammunition that fuels violence. We support the extension of the Multinational Security Support Mission and its mandate to help protect civilians, critical infrastructure and humanitarian access, and to support the Haitian National Police. It is essential that the Mission operates in full compliance with international law, including human rights law and international humanitarian law, and with the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. We also call for full implementation of the sanctions regime and stronger regional and international cooperation against arms trafficking. The United Kingdom welcomes the resolution’s emphasis on a Haitian-led political transition, credible and inclusive elections, and conditions-based planning for any future United Nations role, subject to the consent of the Government of Haiti and a further decision of this Council. We urge Member States to provide sustained and predictable support to the Mission and to the Haitian National Police.
before.United States of America: The United States strongly supports the draft resolution before the Council. Haiti’s security and humanitarian crisis requires sustained, coordinated international action in support of a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned response. This text extends the Multinational Security Support Mission, strengthens protection for civilians and critical infrastructure, reinforces the sanctions and arms-embargo regime, and requests options for more predictable and sustainable financing. We thank Council members for their constructive engagement and urge all Member States and international partners to step up with personnel, equipment, training and contributions. The United States will vote in favour.

after.Panama: Panamá agradece la adopción de esta resolución, que copatrocinamos, y el apoyo unánime del Consejo. La prórroga de la Misión Multinacional de Apoyo a la Seguridad debe traducirse en una protección efectiva de la población civil, en apoyo a la Policía Nacional de Haití, en acceso humanitario sin obstáculos y en una coordinación estrecha con la BINUH y los actores regionales, en pleno respeto de la soberanía y el consentimiento del Estado haitiano. Reiteramos la necesidad de aplicar plenamente el régimen de sanciones y el embargo de armas, de garantizar una financiación previsible y sostenible y de mantener un enfoque basado en los derechos humanos, incluida la debida diligencia, la protección de la niñez y la prevención de la explotación y los abusos sexuales. El objetivo debe ser una transición política haitiana, inclusiva y creíble, que conduzca a elecciones libres y justas cuando las condiciones lo permitan. Cualquier transición futura hacia una operación de mantenimiento de la paz debe ser gradual, basada en condiciones y objeto de una nueva decisión del Consejo. Panamá seguirá apoyando al pueblo y al Gobierno de Haití y a nuestros socios regionales, en particular la CARICOM y la OEA.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United States welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution. We thank Panama, our co-penholder, and all Council members for their constructive engagement. Today’s vote sends a clear message that the Security Council remains united in support of the people of Haiti and in support of a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned response to the crisis.

The United States remains deeply concerned by the worsening security and humanitarian situation, including the expansion of gang control, attacks on civilians and critical infrastructure, and the illicit trafficking of arms and ammunition that continues to fuel violence. This resolution strengthens the Multinational Security Support Mission’s ability to support the Haitian National Police, protect civilians, secure humanitarian access, and help create conditions for a credible political transition.

We stress that full and effective implementation is now essential. We urge all Member States to implement fully the sanctions measures and the arms embargo, and to take concrete action against trafficking networks. We also encourage international stakeholders and donors to step forward with personnel, equipment, training and financing. The Mission cannot succeed without predictable and sustainable support.

The United States remains committed to working with BINUH, the Multinational Security Support Mission, the Haitian authorities, CARICOM, the Organization of American States and other partners to advance a credible, inclusive and participatory political process leading to elections and the seating of a democratically elected president by February 2026, when conditions permit. We will continue to monitor implementation closely and to support accountability for those who fuel violence and undermine Haiti’s stability.
